roles.description: Position Title: Community Organizing and Engagement Intern The Agency You’ll Join: In November 2022, New York City voters overwhelmingly approved three ballot proposals that put racial equity and justice at the heart of city government, including the NYC Commission on Racial Equity (NYC CORE). The first of its kind in the nation, the NYC Commission on Racial Equity is an independent 15-member commission responsible for engaging diverse communities to guide and assess the City’s racial equity planning process. NYC CORE provides accountability for New Yorkers, regularly evaluating the City’s progress on its racial requirements and goals. NYC CORE will be composed of diverse New Yorkers with equity expertise and/or relevant lived experience, serving as a conduit to bring historically excluded communities and voices into government decision-making. The Team You’ll Work With: NYC CORE is an independent commission to hold the NYC government accountable to advance racial equity in government operations and to increase community voice in government decision-making. The Chair & Executive Director is jointly appointed by the Mayor and the New York City Council Speaker. Other NYC CORE commissioners are appointed by the Mayor, City Council Speaker, City Comptroller, and Public Advocate. The Commission's staff is responsible for executing the Commission's day-to-day mission and setting its path to success. NYC CORE team takes the vision of the Chair & Executive Director and the Commissioners and translates it into action strategies and plans that implement accountability for racial equity in the city. Like the Commission itself, the Commission’s staff aims to be representative of New Yorkers from all communities and walks of life. Staff bring an accountability mindset to their work, ensuring they collaborate with city agencies and voice public concerns. The Problems You’ll Solve The Community Organizing and Engagement Intern reports directly to the Director of Community Organizing and Engagement, Cam Morris and the Community Organizing and Engagement team. RESPONSIBILITIES Embeds DEI and racial equity practices and tools into the everyday functioning of the Commission. Monitors and responds to the COE team email for questions, requests, and support needs. Supports team meeting planning, upcoming calendar coordination, and outreach preparation. roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Global Supply Management Team The Global Supply Management Team ensures that Zipline has the parts it needs from suppliers around the world in a reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective way. We build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, negotiate contracts, and monitor supplier performance to reduce supply risk. The team also works closely with the design engineering, supplier industrial engineering, finance, program management, and material management teams to understand part design, manage supply against demand, drive cost reductions, and streamline logistics across international markets. The Role As a Global Supply Management Intern, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the systems, data, and supplier relationships that power Zipline’s global supply chain. You’ll work alongside supply managers, engineers, finance, and operations teams to support sourcing, analytics, and day-to-day execution. This role is perfect for a student to apply classroom knowledge to real-world challenges in procurement, logistics, and global operations. Your work will directly support Zipline’s mission to deliver essential goods and services across the world while building critical skills in supply chain management. What You'll Do Assist in tracking and analyzing supplier performance, purchase orders, and delivery timelines. Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations on supply chain metrics. Support sourcing activities by gathering quotes, conducting supplier research, and benchmarking costs. Work with internal stakeholders to troubleshoot supply issues and identify process improvements. Participate in supplier meetings and cross-functional discussions to gain exposure to real-world negotiations and decision-making. Document and standardize processes to help build scalable systems. What You'll Bring Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable working with spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets). Curiosity and eagerness to learn about global supply chain operations in a fast-paced environment. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work on cross-functional projects. Organizational skills and attention to detail, with a willingness to dive into both strategic and tactical tasks. Preferred majors: Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Economics. What Else You Should Know Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January 2027 to April/May 2027. The hourly rate for this internship is $37 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

roles.title: Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Intern
roles.description: Primary Function of Position The HEOR Intern will join Intuitive’s Future Forward Medical Affairs team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to the Staff Epidemiologist, Future Forward Medical Affairs. The intern will own a defined, scoped real-world evidence project, using administrative claims data and reimbursement coding (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG) to characterize patient populations, procedure volumes, healthcare resource utilization, and costs for a technology in development. Working alongside senior epidemiology, data science, and market access colleagues, the intern will contribute analyses that inform value propositions and may help translate findings into inputs for budget impact or other economic models. The internship culminates in a final presentation to Future Forward leadership and cross-functional partners. Essential Job Duties Real-World Data Analysis: With guidance from senior team members, conduct a retrospective claims-based analysis to characterize patient populations, estimate procedure volumes, and describe utilization, outcomes, and costs relevant to a Future Forward pipeline technology. Coding & Cohort Definition: Identify and validate CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG code sets to define target populations, procedures, comorbidities, and outcomes; document code lists and assumptions so they can be reused by the team. Study Planning & Programming: Contribute to a brief study protocol and statistical analysis plan; write, document, and quality-check analytic code, partnering with the team’s data scientist on shared data pipelines. Evidence Review: Conduct a targeted literature review to inform study design, benchmark findings against published evidence, and surface evidence gaps for the technology under study. Economic Modeling Support: Where relevant, translate claims-based estimates (e.g., procedure volumes, event rates, costs) into inputs for budget impact or other economic models, and support model development or validation. Communication: Summarize findings in clear visualizations and slides; deliver a final presentation to Future Forward leadership; contribute to a draft abstract where findings warrant. Required Skills and Experience Hands-on experience with reimbursement coding systems (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG), gained through dissertation research, research-assistant work, or prior employment, including using codes to define cohorts, procedures, and outcomes. Demonstrated experience analyzing at least one large administrative claims or hospital database (e.g., Medicare MedPAR/SAF, MarketScan, Optum Clinformatics, Premier, PearlDiver, Komodo Health, or similar), from data extraction and cleaning through analysis. Proficiency in SAS and/or R and working knowledge of SQL Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical analysis for non-specialist audiences. Comfortable working on a defined deliverable under the guidance of senior team members, with the independence to drive it to completion within the internship period. Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity; this team works on problems that are not yet fully defined. University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a Health Economics, Health Outcomes/Services Research, Health Policy, Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate (PhD) level. Working Conditions None Preferred Skills and Experience Experience developing or adapting budget impact models or other health economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-consequence) in Excel, consistent with ISPOR good-practice guidelines. Familiarity with Medicare payment methodologies (IPPS/MS-DRG, OPPS/APC, MPFS/RVU) and how coding drives payment across sites of service. Research experience in medical devices, surgery, or procedural care. Peer-reviewed publications or congress abstracts (e.g., ISPOR, AcademyHealth). Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI). Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19. Details can vary by role. Intuitive is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees, and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type, without regard to race, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, color, age, religion, protected veteran or disability status, genetic information or any other status protected under federal, state, or local applicable laws. Mandatory Notices U.S. Export Controls Disclaimer: In accordance with the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR §743.13(b)), some roles at Intuitive Surgical may be subject to U.S. export controls for prospective employees who are nationals from countries currently on embargo or sanctions status. Certain information you provide as part of the application will be used for purposes of determining whether Intuitive Surgical will need to (i) obtain an export license from the U.S. Government on your behalf (note: the government’s licensing process can take 3 to 6+ months) or (ii) implement a Technology Control Plan (“TCP”) (note: typically adds 2 weeks to the hiring process). For any Intuitive role subject to export controls, final offers are contingent upon obtaining an approved export license and/or an executed TCP prior to the prospective employee’s start date, which may or may not be flexible, and within a timeframe that does not unreasonably impede the hiring need. If applicable, candidates will be notified and instructed on any requirements for these purposes. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with fair chance laws. Accommodation & Accessibility Notice: Intuitive is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require assistance or an accommodation during any part of the application or interview process, please contact People Services at . We provide market-competitive compensation packages, inclusive of base pay (paid at an hourly rate), benefits, and a housing allowance. It would not be typical for someone to be hired at the top end of range for the role, as actual pay will be determined based on several factors, including relevant skills and experience for this internship, degree-seeking academic program (PhD, Master’s, Bachelor’s, etc), year in school, and location. The hourly rate is prorated against the intern program salaries listed and total program compensation will be based on internship duration. It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.

roles.title: Human Factors (Winter Co-Op)
roles.description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW: A seaglider floats, foils, and flies — and every one of those transitions has to make sense to the pilots flying it and the passengers riding in it. Nobody has designed that interface before. As a Human Factors Co-Op, you’ll help shape it: contributing to concept sketches, UI/UX standards, and the usability evaluations that keep the interface safe, intuitive, and ready for certification. As part of the Systems team, you’ll be joining a group of driven, collaborative, and talented engineers who take pride in solving complex technical challenges and making an impact as a team. We hold a high bar for engineering rigor, move quickly, think boldly, and rely on our teamwork to push boundaries and bring entirely new technology into the world. If you’d rather sketch and test a real interface than read about one, and you want hands-on experience on a vehicle nobody has built before, we’d love to have you on the team! What You'll Do: - Contribute to new feature concepts. Bring ideas for how pilots and passengers interact with the seaglider human interface. - Help build out our design standards. Contribute to REGENT’s UI/UX standards and design language. - Support safety and usability evaluations. Help plan and run evaluations of the seaglider human interface. - Help define human factors requirements. Support requirements definition and draft test procedures. - Partner across engineering disciplines. Work with engineers across systems, software, and flight test to bring HF findings into the design. What We’re Looking For: - Working toward a relevant degree. Pursuing a degree in Human Factors Engineering, Engineering Psychology, or a related field. - Some exposure to aviation or maritime contexts. Coursework, research, or personal flying, boating, or sailing experience. - Comfort with prototyping and communication. Proficiency with rapid prototyping tools (e.g., Figma); excellent written and verbal communication, including technical documentation. - Self-motivated and adaptable. Comfortable with shifting priorities in a startup environment. Who We’re Looking For: - Curious about people, not just tech. You want to know why someone struggles with an interface, not just that they do, and you’re excited to go find out firsthand. - Hands-on, not just theoretical. You’d rather sketch a quick mockup or run a small usability test than write a memo about what one might find. - Comfortable without a precedent. A seaglider cockpit doesn’t look like anything that exists yet. You’re energized by that, not looking for a template to follow. - Present for the work. Evaluations and test days don’t always land on a tidy schedule, and you’re ready to show up when the work needs you. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we’re looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works. Inventory Manager – High Value Devices Function: Operations – Asset & Inventory Control Inventory Type: High-Value Electronic Assets Tools Used: Manual Registers & Google Sheets Work Mode: On-site Role Overview The Inventory Manager will be responsible for end-to-end custody, tracking, and reconciliation of high-value inventory, primarily iPhones and related accessories such as SD cards and card readers. This role demands strict control, zero tolerance for mismatches, and complete documentation discipline. No inventory movement is allowed without entries, and physical stock must always tally with records. (Morning Shift - 7 am to 4 pm; Evening Shift - 4 pm to 2 am) Key Responsibilities 1. High-Value Inventory Ownership Take complete ownership of high-value devices and accessories . Ensure serial-number–level tracking for all devices. Maintain zero loss and zero undocumented movement . 2. Inward Inventory Management (IT → Inventory) Receive devices and accessories from the IT team. Verify: Quantity Serial numbers Physical condition Record all inward movements immediately in: Manual registers Google Sheets Escalate any mismatch, damage, or discrepancy without delay. 3. Outward Inventory Management (Inventory ↔ Field Ops) Hand over inventory from: Inventory to Field Ops (FO) Field Ops back to Inventory Ensure no item goes out without prior entry . Capture details including: Item name and serial number FO name / ID Date and time of handover Expected return date Avoid all verbal or informal handovers. 4. Returns, Reconciliation & Control Receive returned inventory and re-verify serial numbers and condition. Update return entries on the same day. Perform daily reconciliation between: Physical stock Google Sheets Items with Field Ops Track overdue or missing items and follow up proactively. 5. Documentation & Audit Readiness Maintain clean, structured Google Sheets trackers. Ensure inventory area access is controlled. Support audits and internal checks as required. Maintain high compliance standards for asset handling. Skills & Requirements Mandatory Experience handling high-value inventory or assets . Strong working knowledge of Google Sheets (filters, basic formulas). Experience with manual inventory registers . High attention to detail and accuracy. Preferred Background in inventory, warehouse, logistics, or operations. Experience managing electronic devices or serialized assets. Key Traits Strong ownership and accountability Process-driven with a zero-error mindset High integrity and discipline Comfortable working under strict controls Performance Metrics 100% match between physical inventory and records Zero undocumented inventory movement Zero asset loss due to process lapses Timely reconciliation and reporting Our Values Empathy, Trust & Candor We put ourselves in the shoes of our colleagues and customers and don’t shy away from uncomfortable conversations, instead building trust through honest and direct feedback. roles.title: Market Research Intern – Summer 2027
roles.description: Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures. Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard. We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position POSITION SUMMARY: The National Life Group Internship Program was developed to provide real workplace learning and growth opportunities for undergraduate students. Over the years the program has provided students with the opportunity to engage in meaningful, career-relevant work at National Life Group in preparation for full-time employment. This position currently offers an onsite work schedule, with the expectation that you are in the office four (4) days per week during onsite core days. Our current onsite core days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. The work schedule type and core days are subject to change with advance notification and manager discretion. RESPONSIBILITIES: The Market Research Intern will support projects focused on consumer insights, market sizing, and sales trend analysis. This role provides an opportunity for an undergraduate student to gain hands-on experience working with real business data to inform strategic decisions. The intern will collaborate with cross-functional teams including marketing, distribution, strategy, and product to help uncover insights about customer behavior, market opportunities, and business performance. This position is ideal for a student interested in applying analytical and research skills in a business setting. Assist in analyzing consumer data (customer demographic data, survey data, qualitative interview data) to identify trends and insights Support market sizing and segmentation analyses to evaluate growth opportunities across products, markets, and customer segments Analyze sales performance data to identify trends, drivers of performance, and areas for improvement Help develop presentations and reports that communicate insights clearly to stakeholders Conduct competitive and industry research to inform strategic initiatives Partner with team members to translate data into actionable business recommendations Support ad hoc research and analytics projects across marketing and strategy teams QUALIFICATIONS: Preferred Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, or a related field Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word Ability to interpret data and communicate findings clearly Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Effective written and verbal communication skills Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment Minimum Experience with data analysis tools (e.g., Advanced Excel functions, Tableau, Power BI or R) Familiarity with market research methods (surveys, interviews, focus groups) Interest in financial services, insurance, or consumer behavior Prior internship or project experience involving data analysis or research AI Proficiency Expectations At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength. All associates are expected to: Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work. Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working. Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content. Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products by adhering to National Life's AI guiding principles. Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property. Core Competencies Service Focus - Demonstrates a client centric focus for satisfying one’s external and/or internal customers; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect. Decision Making - Makes sense of complex information, critically evaluates, and creates solutions. Results Oriented - Sets performance and personal goals; Driven to meet or exceed goals and objectives. Plans and Aligns - Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals; Aligns people and skills to tasks and assignments; Evaluates results of work. Demonstrates Learning Agility - Enhances skills and knowledge through continuous learning; Focuses on personal results by establishing stretch goals; Seeks feedback and changes accordingly. Establishes Relationships - Builds partnerships with others to instill trust, collaborate, and meet shared objectives. Communicates Effectively - Actively listens, conveys messages to meet different audience needs, and remains open to new ideas and opinions. Fosters Diversity - Values diversity and difference in thought, experience, and perspective; Promotes an environment that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion; Supports equal and fair treatment for all. HOW YOU SHOW UP: Highly reliable, engaged and possess a customer service attitude Demonstrate effective communication to various areas of the organization (technical and non-technical) Bring creativity, thought leadership, and curiosity to the table; actively participate in forums to contribute and learn Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, i.e. a problem solver’s mindset Eager to learn, ask relevant questions, seek new knowledge, and make connections Enjoy taking on challenges and working towards solutions both collaboratively and independently PROGRAM HIGHLIGHTS: 10-week paid internship (June 1 - August 6) with formal orientation and onboarding Networking opportunities with peers and leaders throughout the summer Cross-Departmental group project focused on an enterprise-wide solution presented at company-wide event Presentation skills coaching sessions Learning opportunities throughout program Access to mentors (former program participants) Base Pay Range . The base pay range for this position is the range National Life reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors, including: prior experience and job-related knowledge; education, training and certificates; current business needs; and market factors. The final salary or hourly wages offered may be outside of this range based on other reasons and individual circumstances. Additional Compensation and Benefits . The total compensation package for this position may also include a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in National Life’s discretionary annual incentive programs, subject to the rules governing such programs. If hired, the employee will be in an "at-will position" and National Life reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. National Life is accepting applications for this role on an ongoing basis and the role remains open until filled. Hourly Pay Range $19 — $28 USD National Life Group® is a trade name of National Life Insurance Company, Montpelier, VT – founded in 1848, Life Insurance Company of the Southwest, Addison, TX – chartered in 1955, and their affiliates. Each company of National Life Group is solely responsible for its own financial condition and contractual obligations. Life Insurance Company of the Southwest is not an authorized insurer in New York and does not conduct insurance business in New York. Equity Services, Inc., Member FINRA/SIPC, is a Broker/Dealer and Registered Investment Adviser affiliate of National Life Insurance Company. All other entities are independent of the companies of National Life Group. Fortune 1000 status is based on the consolidated financial results of all National Life Group companies. roles.title: Operations Intern, Talent Development & Training
roles.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
roles.description: Operations Intern, Talent Development & Training Hillel International Role Overview The Talent Development & Training team is seeking a highly organized, proactive, and collaborative Talent Development Operations Intern to ensure the seamless execution of HillelU’s growing portfolio of professional development programs and experiences. HillelU provides learning and development opportunities to more than 1,200 Hillel professionals across the organization. As our portfolio continues to grow, this role will provide the operational support needed to deliver high-quality professional development experiences consistently and efficiently—from virtual training and cohort programs to immersive in-person leadership development experiences. This role will serve as a key member of the Talent Development & Training team, taking ownership of the systems, logistics, data, and processes that support the participant experience. The ideal candidate is someone who loves turning plans into action, can anticipate details before they become problems, and is energized by making complex programs feel seamless. What You’ll Do Program Operations & Delivery Support the operational execution of assigned HillelU programs and learning experiences, from initial planning through post-program follow-up. Coordinate session setup, registration, materials, technology, and other operational needs. Manage pre- and post-program communications, including reminders, pre-work, and logistics. Provide or coordinate day-of technology and administrative support for virtual and in-person programs. Partner with facilitators and Talent Development colleagues to ensure they have the information and support needed for successful program delivery. Create and maintain repeatable processes, templates, and checklists that make program delivery more efficient and consistent. Identify operational challenges and proactively develop solutions. Program Data, Evaluation & Reporting Collect, organize, maintain and report on participation and program data. Pull and upload data across relevant systems and ensure program records remain accurate and up to date. Coordinate post-program evaluation processes, including evaluation communications and data collection. Develop regular reports and dashboards that help the Talent Development team understand participation, engagement, and program outcomes. Support analysis of program data to identify trends and inform future planning and decision-making. Partner with colleagues to improve how HillelU tracks and communicates program impact. Leadership Development & Event Logistics Support the operational delivery of select high-touch programs and experiences, including Kaplan Supervisory Leadership Program and Accelerate. Coordinate event logistics including hotels, catering, travel, participant communications, materials, schedules, and other event needs. Manage participant travel reimbursements and other program-related expenses. Coordinate across facilitators, participants, vendors, internal partners, and other stakeholders to ensure a seamless experience. Provide on-site operational support for select HillelU professional development experiences, as needed. Systems & Process Improvement Maintain systems for tracking HillelU programs, participants, logistics, and outcomes. Look for opportunities to streamline administrative processes and reduce manual work. Create documentation and standard operating procedures to support consistency and continuity across the HillelU portfolio. Help the team leverage technology and data more effectively in the delivery and evaluation of learning programs. Support implementation of new tools, systems, and processes as HillelU continues to evolve. Team Partnership Serve as a collaborative operational partner to Talent Development colleagues, helping translate program ideas into executable plans. Support multiple concurrent projects and priorities while maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Provide visibility into project status, upcoming deadlines, and operational needs. Take ownership of projects and follow through independently while knowing when to escalate questions or challenges. Contribute to a collaborative, positive, and service-oriented team culture. Who You Are Highly organized and detail-oriented , with the ability to manage many moving pieces without losing sight of the big picture. A strong project manager who can establish timelines, track details, and ensure work moves forward. Proactive and solutions-oriented , with a natural instinct to anticipate needs and troubleshoot challenges. A strong communicator who can build relationships and communicate clearly with a wide range of stakeholders. Comfortable with technology and data , and excited to learn new systems and tools. Service-oriented , with a strong commitment to creating excellent experiences for participants, facilitators, and colleagues. Able to work independently , take ownership, and exercise good judgment. Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple simultaneous priorities. Proficient in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce, Zoom, learning management systems, event platforms, or similar tools is a plus. We encourage both current college students and recent graduates to apply for this role. What You’ll Receive $17/hr up to 20 hours/week In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience in program operations, project coordination, data and evaluation, event logistics, and talent development while working alongside a team that designs and delivers professional development for Hillel professionals across the organization. You’ll have the opportunity to see how learning experiences are designed, delivered, evaluated, and improved and to build skills that translate across nonprofit, education, Human Resources, and business environments. About Hillel International In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.

roles.title: Operations Management Intern
roles.description: Instawork is on a mission to create meaningful economic opportunities for skilled hourly professionals in communities around the globe. Our AI-powered labor marketplace helps local businesses scale, and enables global technology companies to push the frontiers of robotics and AI. Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we’re looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works. Instawork is on a mission to create meaningful economic opportunities for skilled hourly professionals in communities around the globe. Our AI-powered labor marketplace helps local businesses scale, and enables global technology companies to push the frontiers of robotics and AI. Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we're looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works. Role Overview An Internal Coordinator (IC) owns the day-to-day running of field data collection for a single region. Each IC leads a team of Field Officers (FOs) who carry recording rigs(hardware) into partner businesses, set them up correctly, and capture high-quality task recordings. The IC is the operational nerve center of the region: planning the day's pipeline, keeping FOs productive in the field, solving problems live, ensuring recording quality and diversity rules are met, tracking inventory (rigs and SD cards) in and out, and reporting hours planned vs. achieved with clear loss reasons at end of day. This role is mainly about live coordination, field problem-solving, quality control, and disciplined reporting. Who Are Field Officers (FOs)? People working on the ground, out in the field They collect rigs from inventory, travel to assigned businesses, and record short videos of real commercial/household tasks They are responsible for correct setup, on-site recording, and returning rigs and SD cards They have clear daily and overall hour targets to complete Key Responsibilities 1. Start-of-Day Planning Check the day's pipeline of confirmed businesses for each FO Keep enough backup businesses on hand so no FO is left idle if a task falls through Confirm rig, SD card, and inventory availability before FOs leave Plan for exigencies (business cancellations, FO absence, device shortfall, travel issues) 2. Live Monitoring & 2-Hourly Updates Track who has started, who is on-site, who is recording, and who is falling behind Take structured updates from every FO at least every 2 hours to catch and solve issues early Follow up immediately with FOs who are idle, delayed, or stuck 3. Target & Productivity Management Ensure FOs meet their daily and overall hour targets Redirect FOs to backup businesses when a planned task drops, to protect the day's hours Push and motivate the team to close the day on plan 4. Quality, Rules & Diversity Adherence Ensure FOs follow recording rules: correct task type, valid duration, correct rig/camera setup Verify setup quality before recording begins — e.g. confirm camera alignment via screenshots so the rig is capturing correctly before the task runs Ensure recordings respect diversity caps (per-operator and per-environment limits) so hours actually count as usable Work with the Quality team to understand where recordings are failing, and retrain FOs to record better-quality, usable data 5. roles.title: Payroll & Benefits Intern (Practicante de Nómina y Compensación)
roles.description: The salary for the Payroll & Benefits Intern is $2.800.000 COP monthly. About Sezzle With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role As a Payroll & Benefits Intern, you'll join our People Operations team and work directly with our Senior Director of Payroll & Benefits. You'll see how payroll, compensation, and benefits run across Colombia, the United States, and Canada inside a fast-growing, publicly traded fintech. This is a paid, learning-focused internship with a clear path to full-time conversion based on performance. We are seeking a talented and motivated intern who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. No prior payroll experience is required; attention to detail, curiosity, and a good head for numbers matter more. What You'll Do Help run monthly payroll: data entry, reconciliations, and documentation Keep payroll, benefits, and HR system data accurate, and flag anything that doesn't match Support benefits enrollments, changes, and employee records Help prepare documents for monthly, quarterly, and year-end audits Gather market data for compensation benchmarking Answer employee questions about payroll and benefits Spot manual steps we can automate, including testing new AI tools What You'll Learn How multi-country payroll works, from Colombian labor law to US payroll and benefits rules (FLSA, ACA, ERISA, COBRA) How companies benchmark and set compensation How People Operations supports a company's growth, including Sezzle's bank charter readiness What We Look For Current university student or recent graduate in Accounting (Contaduría Pública), Finance, Economics, Business Administration, Industrial Engineering, or a related field Strong attention to detail and comfort working with numbers Good Excel or Google Sheets skills English proficiency (written and spoken), since you'll work daily with US-based teams Native or near-native Spanish Discretion with confidential information Comfortable using AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to boost productivity, research, and communication Nice to Have Coursework or basic knowledge of Colombian payroll, taxes, or labor regulations Interest in automation and process improvement About You You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. Compensation: The salary for the Payroll & Benefits Intern is $2.800.000 COP monthly. #Li-remote #Full-time

The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . This is a 12-week internship during summer 2027. You'll join the People Analytics team within our People Success Function. This team provides intelligence and tools that empower leaders to make key people decisions and drive business value. You'll support analyses across the employee lifecycle, help streamline reporting processes, and contribute to solutions that measure the impact of complex People programs. roles.title: People Center Intern – Summer 2027
roles.description: Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures. Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard. We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position POSITION SUMMARY: As an intern in the People Center, you will have the opportunity to learn about each of the critical functions within Human Resources that shape the employee experience at National Life. You will rotate through two areas of the People Center, gaining hands on experience in Talent Acquisition, Learning & Organizational Development. Throughout this rotation, you will work on meaningful projects that impact our programs and processes in partnership with business leaders on the People team. If you're interested in a career at National Life, this internship is a great way to begin your journey! KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: The People Center intern will be a vital part of our team and will contribute to our continuing efforts to identify and implement best practices. Key projects include: job posting and resume reviews, recruiting advertising campaign support, content mapping of Servant Leadership, partnership in extended onboarding curriculum and candidate experience. QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum overall GPA of 3.00 Working towards a degree in Human Resources Management, rising Senior preferred Coursework in human resources, organizational development, communications, or related area preferred Proficient in Microsoft tools with interest in learning new tools and systems Excellent written and verbal communication skills. AI Proficiency Expectations: At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. You'll work directly with the head of AI Transformation & People Strategy, alongside HR leaders, process owners and engineers. roles.description: About Us SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja , the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. AI at SharkNinja At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. roles.title: Product User Research, Intern
roles.description: ABOUT SARVAM AI Sarvam AI is building India's sovereign AI stack, spanning foundational models, infrastructure and applications. Our mission is to make powerful AI accessible and useful for India, building technology that works across languages, industries and real-world use cases. As we continue to build and scale our products, understanding how people interact with them becomes increasingly important. We're looking for a curious and research-oriented intern to help us understand our users better and shape the experiences we build. THE ROLE As a Product User Research Intern, you'll work closely with our product, design and engineering teams to understand user behaviour, identify friction points and uncover opportunities to improve our products. You'll interact directly with developers, product managers and founders, study how they use Sarvam's products, and translate your findings into actionable insights that influence product and design decisions. This is an opportunity to work on a new user research function at Sarvam, helping establish research practices and processes from the ground up. You'll also get ownership of a primary product area and the opportunity to see your research translate into real product improvements. WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON - Understand our users: Conduct user interviews, surveys and usability studies with developers, PMs and founders to understand their needs, behaviours and challenges. - Improve product experiences: Research user journeys across Sarvam's developer console, playground, API documentation and applications. Identify friction points across onboarding, API key creation, first API calls, billing and other key workflows. - Study developer journeys: Analyse the developer funnel, from sign-up to making the first API call and eventually becoming a paying user. Understand where users drop off and, more importantly, why. - Test and evaluate designs: Conduct usability testing on existing interfaces and new prototypes, run preference and A/B tests, and benchmark experiences against other developer products. - Turn research into insights: Analyse qualitative and quantitative data, identify patterns and present clear recommendations to product, design, growth and support teams. - Build the research practice: Help establish research playbooks, interview templates, participant recruitment processes and a research repository that can scale with the team. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Strong curiosity about user behaviour and a genuine interest in understanding why people use products the way they do. - Comfortable speaking with users, conducting interviews and asking thoughtful, unbiased questions. - Technical fluency — you should be comfortable reading API documentation, making basic API calls using tools like Postman, curl or Python, and understanding what might have gone wrong when an API fails. - Comfortable working with data, analysing spreadsheets and interpreting product funnels or dashboards. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate research findings into clear insights and recommendations. - Familiarity with AI tools and developer products, and an interest in exploring how they can improve research workflows. roles.title: Program Management Intern
roles.description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's Paladin test program is where engineering development, vehicle maintenance, and on-water testing all converge, and this internship sits right at the center of it. You'll build and maintain the schedule that the entire program runs on, working directly with the vehicle and the test team rather than tracking progress from behind a desk. This is a DPM-style role in the truest sense: the milestone tracker isn't a document you update once a week, it's something you actively manage so that engineers, maintenance crews, and test leads are always working from the same plan. You'll join the Engineering & Technology Program Management team, a group that treats planning and tracking as real engineering work, not administrative overhead. Along the way, you'll be taught to see cost and schedule as engineering variables in their own right, a lens that's genuinely valuable whether you're headed toward program leadership or engineering management down the road. If you're someone who gets energized by being in the middle of the action, who sees a plan as something to steer rather than observe, and who wants hands-on exposure to how a real flight test program comes together, we'd love to have you on the team. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the Master Schedule: You'll build and keep current the milestone tracker that ties together engineering, maintenance, and on-water testing for Paladin. This is a living document you actively manage, not something you dust off weekly. - Get Hands-On with Paladin: You'll spend real time with the vehicle and the test team, not just behind a laptop. Being in the mix is how you'll understand what's actually happening on the ground, not just what's on paper. - Support Vehicle Maintenance: You'll pitch in on maintenance work between test runs, giving you direct insight into what keeps Paladin flight-ready. That proximity to the vehicle is what makes your tracking actually useful. - Know What Complete Really Means: You'll learn to distinguish between a part being ordered, installed, and tested, so your schedule reflects reality rather than optimism. That distinction is what keeps the whole program honest. - Keep the Team Aligned: You'll make sure engineering, maintenance, and test ops are working from the same set of assumptions about what's next. When the plan stays current, the whole program moves faster together. - Launch Your Own Initiatives: You'll take on program initiatives you can plan, manage, and see through to completion. By the end of your term, you'll be able to point to specific projects you drove start to finish. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Scheduling Tool Fluency: You're comfortable in Smartsheet, MS Project, Jira, or a similar tool. The specific platform matters less than being able to hit the ground organizing the program instead of learning software. - Self-Directed Ownership: You can build and maintain a tracker across multiple workstreams without someone feeding you updates. You treat the plan as something to manage proactively, not react to. - Mechanical Curiosity: Hands-on experience with engines, hulls, or mechanical systems, whether through marine, automotive, or other tinkering, gives you a head start here. A meaningful part of this role involves real vehicle maintenance support. - Technical Grounding: You understand what an engineering or test milestone actually means when it's marked complete. That understanding is what keeps a schedule accurate instead of just looking fine on paper. - Comfort Across Contexts: You're just as comfortable updating a tracker as you are standing next to the vehicle with the test team. You don't need the two worlds kept separate. - Natural Organizational Instinct: You bring structure to dynamic, fast-moving work without slowing it down. You see a plan as something worth actively shaping. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

roles.title: Research Intern (Academic Credit) - Karsh Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology - Per Diem (On-site)
roles.description: About Us: We are a leading research institution committed to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. Our team is dedicated to conducting ground breaking research and providing meaningful learning opportunities for aspiring scientists. Join us and contribute to our mission while gaining invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment. The Research Internship program provides students and trainees an opportunity to develop basic research skills. Interns in this program are provided the opportunity to experience and observe many different aspects of basic, translational and/or clinical research. This program offers interns a unique experience, which is intended to provide a wealth of knowledge about the numerous options for a career in healthcare research. Typically lasting not more than a twelve-month period, this internship will expose participants to a diverse spectrum of clinical and non-clinical based research investigations. Under direct supervision from the assigned Postdoctoral Scientist, senior-level Research Associate and/or Principal Investigator, the intern will be provided with basic research instruction, will be oriented to the Institutional Review Board and other Human Subjects courses, and will be introduced to new and innovative research practices and techniques. Overview of Department & Mentor The Karsh Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at Cedars-Sinai provides comprehensive clinical care and conducts clinical and translational research in liver disease, including alcohol-associated liver disease, metabolic liver disease, cirrhosis, and liver transplantation. The research program includes observational and prospective clinical studies focused on disease outcomes, risk prediction, biomarkers, and clinical data analysis. The intern will enroll under Judong Yang, MD on their course contract, and directly mentored and supervised by Hyunseok Kim, MD, MPH, PhD, a transplant hepatologist whose research focuses on alcohol-associated liver disease and clinical outcomes research. Role Summary & Objectives This research internship will provide UCLA students receiving academic credit with a structured educational experience in clinical hepatology research. Under faculty supervision, the intern will learn principles of clinical research methodology, human-subjects research, literature review, clinical data collection and abstraction, research database management, data quality assessment, basic statistical analysis, and interpretation of research findings. The intern will gain experience in developing research questions and understanding how clinical data are used to investigate outcomes in patients with liver disease. Depending on progress and interest, the intern may also participate in preparation of research presentations, abstracts, and manuscripts. Role Activities & Timeline Weeks 1-2: Orientation to the research program, research objectives, study protocols, responsible conduct of research, patient confidentiality, and applicable IRB requirements. Training in approved Cedars-Sinai research systems and databases as appropriate. Weeks 3-6: Supervised literature review and clinical research data abstraction and organization for approved hepatology research projects. Training in data definitions, data quality control, and maintenance of research databases. Weeks 7-10: Continued supervised data collection and quality assessment, introduction to basic data analysis, and discussion of interpretation of clinical research findings. Weeks 11-12: and ongoing: Review and interpretation of findings with the research team. Depending on the student's progress, participation in preparation of research summaries, presentations, abstracts, and/or manuscripts. The intern will meet regularly with the direct supervisor and/or research team for mentorship, review of progress, research education, and feedback throughout the appointment. Required Education & Experience • Must be 18 years of age or older. • Must have a HS Diploma or GED. • Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern or visitor appointment. • INTERNS: Those participating for academic credit must receive academic credit for the duration of the internship. Preferred Education & Experience Current undergraduate or graduate student enrolled at UCLA and eligible to receive academic credit for the internship. Interest in Medicine, Biology, Public Health, Epidemiology, Data Science, or clinical research is preferred. Strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills are desirable. Prior experience with clinical research, statistics, data management, or scientific literature review is helpful but not required.

While the majority of time is spent apprenticing staff-level roles, there is also an opportunity to understand management level functions which can include hiring, training, coaching, inventory management and P&L oversight. Previous experience working in restaurants is helpful, but not a prerequisite. Intern placements will be determined by fit and assigned to an operating team in one of the restaurants around the country, with a strong focus on East Hampton, NY and Aspen, CO. Compensation will vary based on location but typically average $1200-$1800/week. Hillstone Restaurant Group is a privately-held collection of upscale restaurants with 45+ locations in vibrant cities across the country. Some of our more well-known operations are Houston’s, Hillstone, R+D Kitchen, Bandera, East Hampton Grill, South Beverly Grill, Honor Bar, Palm Beach Grill, and White House Tavern. To learn more, visit us at , or read this profile in Bon Appetit magazine: Placement for the internship is decided upon hire, based on fit to the operating team. This might not be in Aspen, CO, as we have 38 properties around the United States, making relocation contingent upon employment. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The Hillstone Restaurant Group confirms each employee’s identity and authorization to work by participating in E-Verify.

roles.title: SG Campus Recruitment - Localization QA (LQA) Intern
roles.description: About Company： As a leading internet technology company based in China, NetEase, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTES and HKEX:9999, “NetEase”) provides premium online services centered around content creation. With extensive offerings across its expanding gaming ecosystem, the Company develops and operates some of China’s most popular and longest-running mobile and PC games. Powered by industry-leading in-house R&D capabilities in China and globally, NetEase creates superior gaming experiences, inspires players, and passionately delivers value for its thriving community worldwide. By infusing play with culture and education with technology, NetEase transforms gaming into a meaningful vehicle to build a more entertaining and enlightened world. NetEase’s ESG initiatives are among the best in the global media and entertainment industry, earning it a distinction as one of the S&P Global Industry Movers and an “A” rating from MSCI. For more information, please visit: http://ir.netease.com/ Position Overview： Responsible for localization quality assurance of the product in overseas target markets, ensuring localized text is accurate, contextually natural, culturally adapted and free of dissonance. The last line of defense for "copy-as-product" quality in overseas publishing. Responsibilities： Conduct language and functional testing of localized versions of in-game text, UI, events and narratives Review translations from a native target-market perspective; correct stiff translations, cultural inappropriateness and tone deviations Log and track localization bugs (text truncation / variable misplacement / encoding issues / contextual errors) Verify text consistency and compliance across language / region versions (e.g., rating language) Coordinate with localization and worldview/narrative teams; provide feedback on how narratives land in target languages Requirements: Currently enrolled or fresh graduate; majors in Language / Translation / Media / Game / Digital Media preferred, any major acceptable Native-level proficiency in target-market languages (English, and/or French / German / Spanish / Portuguese and other European / American languages) Sensitive to target-market culture, slang and gaming terminology Meticulous and patient with strong quality awareness; able to log issues systematically Casual / merge game player experience preferred Preferred Qualifications: Experience in localization / translation / QA / game testing Second or third language proficiency to cover multilingual testing Familiarity with localization tools or bug tracking systems (e.g., Jira) Fair Employment Practices At NetEase, we are committed to fair employment practices. We welcome applications from all individuals, irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability.

roles.title: Sourcing Program Management Intern (Winter/Spring 2027)
roles.description: Do you want to change how the world creates? At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before. We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us. Your Impact: The components we source from all over the world are essential to the success of our products and company. We must carefully balance our need to lower costs while ensuring high performance, reliability, and abundant supply. You’ll work with our team of engineers to build relationships with suppliers and expand the capabilities of Formlabs to directly improve our products. This internship offers hands-on experience in supply chain management, strategic sourcing, procurement processes, and the successful introduction of new products into the market. If you are focused and inspired with a passion for streamlining and optimization, we want you as a Global Sourcing Intern on our Global Sourcing Team. Internship Term: Winter/Spring 2027 (January-April) Commitment: Full-time Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA The Job: Work directly with current and potential suppliers to keep our material pipeline flowing. Support supply chain risk assessments and contingency planning. Develop strategies to better optimize our suppliers for cost, quality, and supply resilience. Conduct market analysis to provide deep and meaningful sourcing insights. Support the team in managing purchase orders, invoices, and supplier communications. Supplier sourcing, qualification, and negotiation processes. Collaborate with engineering teams and manufacturers to ensure timely development builds and transition to mass production. You: Have a technical or engineering background. Excited to source, contact, and evaluate potential suppliers for quality, reliability, cost and capacity. Able to work with a variety of teams, communicating effectively in-person and remotely. Organized and focused, able to handle concurrent conversations and projects, documenting progress along the way. Leadership experience and exposure to project management. Eagerness to learn and adapt to new challenges. Bonus Skills (Optional): Manufacturing and procurement experience Advanced use of Microsoft Excel Product development experience Familiarity with part inspection and corrective action, i.e. Quality Control Experience with the manufacturing technologies used to make our printer parts: injection molding, machining, sheet metal stamping, bending, and forming, SMT etc. Intern Benefits & Perks: Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it Salaried bi-weekly pay schedule Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community And of course… unlimited 3D prints We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing. Compensation: Interns at Formlabs are paid on a bi-weekly pay schedule. The pay range for this role will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. This is a salaried role, so you will always be paid based on the assumed 40 hours per week as a full-time intern. This position does not offer housing or relocation assistance. The weekly pay range for this role is: $1,575 — $1,950 USD
